sentences.text: Task 3. Cherry is now talking to a group of Form 5 and 6 students about the college’s online systems and issues about studying online.
Complete the information in the spaces provided as you listen.
One has been done for you as an example.
You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task, you will have one and a half minutes to tidy up your answers.
OK, thanks everyone for coming.
I hope you don't mind me recording this?
Perhaps we can start with everybody saying a little bit about what they think the main issues are about, you know, studying online at Aberdeen College Right, well, I can start.
I think I should say from the outset that there’s no way you can replace real learning in a classroom with reading from websites and watching videos on YouTube Sorry, can you introduce yourself?
Oh, sorry, I'm Grace Yao from 5C.
OK, Grace, please go on.
You were saying that learning online can’t replace classroom learning.
Yeah, I mean, learning is meant to be interactive, right?
We learn from teachers and we learn from classmates.
We learn by listening to people who know more than us like the teacher and by talking to people who are learning along with us.
We also learn by doing things.
Like in science, we learn by doing experiments and in art we learn by creating things.
You can create things on computers as well.
Yeah, but it’s not the same, dough, is it?
I think computers and iPads and iPhones are brilliant for playing games and chatting with our friends and stuff, but it’s not real learning is it?
OK, maybe you can tell us more about what you think.
What's your name again?
Me? My name’s Icarus Liu Icarus, that’s an unusual name, how do you spell that?
I -C -A -R -U -S Icarus Liu How are you?
OK, Icarus, what do you think?
Well, I mean, we all have computers at home and a lot of students have laptops as well so we can all access online learning materials so I think we should be using that environment
to learn much more than we do.
To be honest, I learn more at home than at school That’s quite a bold statement there, Icarus.
Yeah. I mean, there’s lots of ways we can learn online We can use video conferencing to talk to people and we can use all kinds of creative software What do you mean creative software
creative software you know to draw or design things Oh, right.
OK. Right maybe I'll ask somebody else.
Yes Yeah, hi, I’m Michael Ong from 6B.
Obviously I haven't thought about this as much as Grace and Icarus.
I’m still not sure about all this really I mean, I can now be reading, you know a book or whatever, and I can look up any words I don’t know on an online dictionary instantly and learn that way.
But I still want to share what I've learned with my classmates mates as well and get my teacher's advised on how to use it.
OK, I want to switch the focus of our discussion a little now and ask how you'd feel about having a facility that lets students and teachers communicate with each other.
We can do that already through Facebook.
Why not just have a College Facebook page?
That's an option we've talked about.
Do you think it would be a good idea?
No, I think it’s too dangerous.
Students are too keen to put themselves on Facebook.
They post all sorts of personal stuff like, I don't know they put up videos of themselves and they give out their phone number.
I just think it’s dangerous, Dangerous?
Dangerous how Grace?
Because you don’t know who’s going to be reading all of this personal stuff.
I mean if you do post your phone number, it’s really stupid.
Yeah, but you can control who sees your information.
I know. I know you can But a lot of students just don’t bother and they say yes to every friend request, even if they don’t know that person.
OK, fine. There are always dangers.
I would never give out personal information like my home address or whatever.
But often people do.
That's the point.
I think some students are just too eager to make new friends No, the point is that people need to learn that doing that sort of thing is stupid Michael?
I tend to agree with Icarus.
Making friends online is one of the great benefits of having an online social network.
network. It’s part of the reality of the outside world.
The school should get a social network and then take the opportunity to educate students about the dangers.
Not just pretend that the dangers don’t exist.
Totally. Yeah. Use technology to educate students about the dangers.
Yeah That is the end of Task 3.
